stories.title: Fashion Brand Veronica Beard Expands Headquarters Space
stories.excerpt: Fashion brand Veronica Beard has renewed and expanded its headquarters lease at 26 W. 17th St. in Manhattan to approximately 60,000 square feet, growing its footprint by 15,000 square feet. It now will occupy the entire second, third, fifth, sixth, seventh and eighth floors. The CBRE team of David Stockel and Taylor Walker led the leasing campaign and represented ownership, The Winter Organization, in lease negotiations. TJ Hochanadel and Rob Martin of JLL represented Veronica Beard. “Veronica Beard’s decision to renew and expand its footprint at 26 W. 17th St. demonstrates confidence in both the location and its future growth trajectory,” said Stockel. “The transaction highlights continued demand from established tenants for high-quality office environments that support collaboration, culture and business expansion. The post Fashion Brand Veronica Beard Expands Headquarters Space appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Veronica Beard expands Manhattan HQ 15K SF to 60K SF total at 26 W. 17th St.
Fashion/apparel tenant renews and grows footprint, signaling confidence in Chelsea office market.
Established fashion brand prioritizes high-quality, collaborative office environment for retention and expansion.
stories.summary: Fashion brand Veronica Beard renewed and expanded its headquarters lease at 26 W. 17th St. in Manhattan, growing from 45,000 to 60,000 square feet and occupying six full floors. The decision signals tenant confidence in the Chelsea location and demand for premium office space supporting company culture and growth. CBRE and JLL brokered the transaction.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. Office leasing strength in Manhattan's Chelsea submarket may indicate broader economic confidence in the market, but does not materially affect apartment demand, supply, or development economics.

stories.title: Paladin Expands SoCal Workforce Portfolio with Bellflower Acquisition
stories.excerpt: Paladin Realty Partners LLC, has expanded its growing workforce rental housing portfolio in Southern California with the recent acquisition of Brownstone Apartments, a 17-unit apartment community located in Bellflower. Built in 1967, the property has nine one-bedroom units, seven two-bedroom units and a studio unit. As with its previous SoCal workforce housing investments, Paladin intends to pursue a value-added business plan to modernize the property. “While on the smaller side for us, Brownstone Apartments is exactly the type of opportunity we seek in Southern California,” said Fred Gortner, Co-Founder and Head of U.S. Strategy at Paladin Realty. “It’s a well-located, well-maintained but under-managed asset in a prime workforce housing submarket. Our objective is to upgrade the asset and enhance the residents’ quality of life, while preserving critically needed affordable workforce housing in a highly desirable infill location.” California Bank & Trust provided the debt financing. Bridgeport Investments in Newport Beach served as a financial advisor to Paladin. Tracy Hong and Chris Keramati at Trigor Group brokered the transaction. The post Paladin Expands SoCal Workforce Portfolio with Bellflower Acquisition appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Paladin Realty acquires 17-unit Brownstone Apartments in Bellflower, California for workforce housing.
Built 1967; under-managed asset targeted for value-add modernization and resident quality improvement.
Paladin expanding SoCal workforce housing portfolio with smaller, well-located in-fill opportunities.
stories.summary: Paladin Realty Partners acquired Brownstone Apartments, a 17-unit Class-C community in Bellflower, California built in 1967, containing nine one-bedroom, seven two-bedroom, and one studio unit. The acquisition continues Paladin's focus on workforce housing in Southern California through a value-add strategy targeting under-managed, well-maintained assets. California Bank & Trust provided debt financing.
stories.impact: Signals persistent investor appetite for workforce housing acquisition and value-add repositioning in Southern California, particularly Inland Empire adjacent submarkets, even at small unit counts. Trend suggests rents and NOI recovery justify renovation capex; underscores feasibility of smaller-scale repositioning plays in SoCal's affordable/workforce segment.

stories.title: Walker & Dunlop Arranges Refi on Newly Built Bed-Stuy Multifamily
stories.excerpt: Walker & Dunlop, Inc. arranged a $137.5-million refinancing for 12 Halsey, a newly completed Class A mixed-use multifamily property located in Brooklyn’s Bedford-Stuyvesant neighborhood. Walker & Dunlop Capital Markets Institutional Advisory advised EJS Group and Hope Street Capital in arranging the three-year, floating-rate financing with AllianceBernstein. Aaron Appel, Jonathan Schwartz, Keith Kurland, Adam Schwartz, Dustin Stolly, Sean Reimer, Michael Diaz, Michael Ianno, and Cole Grims led the refinancing. “Demand for newly constructed multifamily assets in New York City remains exceptionally strong, particularly for properties that combine high-quality execution, affordability, and transit-oriented locations,” said Appel. “12 Halsey represents exactly the type of institutional-quality asset that continues to attract significant lender interest.” Completed in October 2025, 12 Halsey comprises 240 residential units, with 30% designated as affordable, along with approximately 2,400 square feet of ground-floor retail. The property occupies a full cross-block site between Fulton and Halsey streets and benefits from immediate access to the A and C subway lines. The post Walker & Dunlop Arranges Refi on Newly Built Bed-Stuy Multifamily appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Walker & Dunlop arranges $137.5M refi for 12 Halsey, 240-unit new Class A in Bed-Stuy, Brooklyn.
30% affordable units, completed Oct 2025, full-block site with direct A/C subway access.
Strong lender demand for transit-oriented, mixed-income institutional-quality multifamily in NYC.
stories.summary: Walker & Dunlop arranged a $137.5 million three-year floating-rate refinancing for 12 Halsey, a newly completed 240-unit mixed-use multifamily property in Brooklyn's Bed-Stuyvesant neighborhood. The property includes 30% affordable units, 2,400 SF of ground-floor retail, and occupies a full cross-block site with immediate access to A and C subway lines. AllianceBernstein provided the institutional financing.
stories.impact: Strong post-completion refi pricing on newly built transit-oriented multifamily with affordable components confirms sustained institutional capital appetite for NYC multifamily despite recent market volatility. Bed-Stuy's transit connectivity and affordability mix command premium lender support, validating development feasibility and encouraging similar transit + affordability-focused development in outer-borough submarkets with strong connectivity.

stories.title: IPA Team Closes Sale of Pomona Multifamily
stories.excerpt: Institutional Property Advisors (IPA), a division of Marcus & Millichap dedicated to serving the company’s institutional clients, closed the sale of Terramonte at Foothill, a 138-unit multifamily asset in Pomona. The $36.7-million sale price represents $265,942 per unit. “The sale is one of only four 100-plus-unit, market-rate multifamily transactions to have occurred in Pomona over the past five years,” said Kevin Green IPA executive director. Green, Zorbas, Joseph Grabiec, Alexander Garcia Jr., and Greg Harris of IPA represented the seller, Positive Investments, and procured the buyer, Sack Capital Partners. The property is located on Foothill Boulevard/State Route 66 off State Route 210, near Interstate 10. These freeways, and the nearby Montclair TransCenter, Pomona Transit Center, and Pomona-North Metrolink station give residents transportation options to employment centers in Los Angeles and throughout the Inland Empire. California State Polytechnic University, Pomona, the University of La Verne, Western University of Health Sciences, and the Claremont Colleges surround the property. The post IPA Team Closes Sale of Pomona Multifamily appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: IPA closes $36.7M sale of 138-unit Terramonte at Foothill in Pomona; $265K per unit price.
Only fourth 100+ unit market-rate transaction in Pomona in past five years; near I-10, Metrolink, universities.
Strong buyer demand (Sack Capital) for transit-accessible workforce housing in Inland Empire.
stories.summary: Institutional Property Advisors closed the sale of Terramonte at Foothill, a 138-unit market-rate multifamily asset in Pomona, for $36.7 million ($265,942 per unit). The property is located on Foothill Boulevard near I-10, close to Pomona Transit Center, Pomona-North Metrolink station, and four universities. The sale represents only the fourth 100+ unit market-rate multifamily transaction in Pomona over the past five years.
stories.impact: Scarcity of 100+ unit transactions in Pomona over five years signals either limited new supply, tight hold periods, or investor caution in the submarket despite transit access and university anchors. Buyer interest (Sack Capital) at ~$266K/unit in this undertraded market may indicate acquisition opportunity ahead of Inland Empire rent growth driven by LA employment spillover and transit-oriented development demand.

stories.title: BFC, SAA Canopy Land $269M Financing for Syracuse Redevelopment
stories.excerpt: BFC Partners and SAA Canopy Group have closed on a $269-million construction loan to transform the long-standing Parkside Commons housing complex on Syracuse’s East Side. The project will deliver a total of 393 affordable apartments through a combination of renovated and newly constructed housing. “Our mission at BFC is to create high-quality affordable housing that enhances the quality of life for the families who call our communities home,” said Winthrop Wharton, principal, BFC Partners. “Parkside Commons is poised for a transformative new chapter, and we are proud to partner with New York State to deliver the substantial investments this community deserves.” The property currently consists of 10 buildings spanning Westmoreland and East Fayette Streets, and the loan will enable BFC Partners and SAA Canopy to simultaneously renovate six of those buildings and construct two new ones. The new buildings will provide enough space to relocate every current resident of the four oldest structures on the site, which will then be demolished. Once that land is cleared, it will become the site of additional housing in a later development phase. The post BFC, SAA Canopy Land $269M Financing for Syracuse Redevelopment appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: BFC Partners and SAA Canopy close $269M construction loan for Parkside Commons redevelopment in Syracuse.
393 total affordable apartments: 6 buildings renovated, 2 new constructed; 4 oldest demolished and future phase.
Major NYS-backed investment in affordable housing redevelopment in secondary market.
stories.summary: BFC Partners and SAA Canopy Group closed a $269 million construction loan to transform Parkside Commons, a long-standing housing complex on Syracuse's East Side. The project will deliver 393 affordable apartments through simultaneous renovation of six existing buildings and construction of two new ones. The loan will enable demolition of four oldest structures, clearing land for additional housing in a future phase.
stories.impact: Large state-backed construction capital flowing into affordable redevelopment in secondary market (Syracuse) signals strong public investment in distressed housing stock remediation. Projects of this scale and complexity (simultaneous renovation, relocation, demolition, phased new construction) demonstrate feasibility of transformative mid-market affordable development, though financing structure and timeline require patient capital and public subsidy alignment—not typical market-rate development model.

stories.title: TekSynap Leases 27K SF at BXP’s Reston Town Center
stories.excerpt: Federal IT contractor TekSynap has signed a long-term lease for a 26,500-square-foot floor at BXP’s Reston Town Center in Northern Virginia. TekSynap provides cloud integration, cybersecurity, software development and IT modernization services for civilian, defense and intelligence agencies. The Reston-based company will relocate less than a mile from 1900 Oracle Way to the second floor of 11921 Freedom Drive. The new office will house TekSynap’s core services team and serve as what the company described as a digital nerve center for its operations. TekSynap employs about 1,800 people, including subcontractors. The transaction marks another office lease at BXP’s 5 million-square-foot Reston Town Center mixed-use campus. “TekSynap’s move to Reston Town Center underscores the demand for workplaces that combine high-quality office space with a vibrant, amenity-rich environment,” Erin Cotter, BXP’s vice president of office leasing, said in a statement. TekSynap CEO Kam Jinnah said the relocation reflects the company’s rapid expansion in the government technology sector, particularly as artificial intelligence reshapes information technology. “Our growth has not come easily; it has been earned through technical excellence, responsiveness, and an unwavering commitment to our customers’ missions,” Jinnah said in a statement. “Taking major space in the heart of the Reston Town Center is a meaningful milestone for our company.” Cole Spalding of Newmark represented TekSynap in the lease and announced the deal on Monday. Reston Town Center includes approximately 50 retailers, more than 30 restaurants and a newer expansion adjacent to the Silver Line’s Metro station with two office towers, the 39-story Skymark apartment tower, dual-branded Marriott hotels and 60,000 square feet of retail. bullets: TekSynap (fed IT contractor, ~1,800 employees) leases 26.5K SF at Boston Properties' Reston Town Center.
Relocation less than 1 mile from Oracle Way; serves as digital nerve center for core services team.
Continued office leasing strength at mixed-use transit hub in Northern Virginia federal corridor.
stories.summary: Federal IT contractor TekSynap signed a long-term lease for 26,500 square feet at Boston Properties' Reston Town Center in Northern Virginia, relocating less than a mile from its prior location at 1900 Oracle Way. TekSynap employs approximately 1,800 people including subcontractors and provides cloud integration, cybersecurity, and IT modernization services to civilian, defense, and intelligence agencies. The move reflects the company's rapid expansion.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. However, sustained office leasing by federal contractors in Reston Town Center (mixed-use amenity hub) signals ongoing employer stability and job growth in Northern Virginia federal/defense IT sector, which underpins rental demand in Reston and surrounding submarkets. Longer-term: federal contractor expansion in DC-NoVA corridor supports steady multifamily demand from highly-paid workforce.

stories.title: University of California Buys 16 Westwood Village Properties for $50M
stories.excerpt: The University of California is extending its streak of commercial real estate investment after acquiring a 16-property portfolio immediately south of UCLA in Los Angeles. The Regents of the University of California, which governs the state’s university system, put down $49.8 million for the properties in Westwood Village, Atlas Brief reported. The portfolio includes 181,855 square feet of retail, office and open space on about 2.6 acres mostly along Westwood Boulevard, as well as on Kinross Avenue, Gayley Avenue and Lindbrook Drive. One property at 1000-1010 Westwood Boulevard spans 64,491 square feet and traded for about $5.75 million, or $89 per square foot. Another property, the historic Kinross Cornerstone, was built in 1930, but has been renovated. No specific plan for the properties has been publicly announced. Representatives for UC Regents did not immediately return a request for comment. Anderson Real Estate, the family-owned real estate company tied to the late John E. Anderson, sold the portfolio. The Anderson family gave more than $140 million to UCLA, built the business organization that included Topa Equities, and co-founded investment firm Kayne Anderson. UCLA’s business school is named after Anderson. The portfolio gives the Regents more commercial assets on the Westside, one of L.A.’s most difficult markets for assembling land. UCLA is transforming the former Westside Pavilion into a 700,000-square-foot research park after acquiring the property for $700 million two and a half years ago. UCLA also acquired Downtown L.A.’s historic 334,000-square-foot Trust Building three years ago to expand classrooms and administrative offices. And, in November 2024, UCLA paid $55 million for a 170,000-square-foot South Bay office property for a $90 million redevelopment into the UCLA Health Sports Medicine Institute. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: UC Regents acquire 16-property portfolio in Westwood Village, LA for $49.8M; 181K SF retail/office/open space.
Strategic land assemblage immediately south of UCLA campus on ~2.6 acres; no redevelopment plan announced.
Institutional buyer repositioning commercial properties adjacent to major university anchor.
stories.summary: The University of California Regents acquired a 16-property portfolio in Westwood Village for $49.8 million, comprising approximately 181,855 square feet of retail, office, and open space on 2.6 acres south of the UCLA campus. Properties are located along Westwood Boulevard, Kinross, Gayley, and Lindbrook avenues. No specific redevelopment plan has been publicly announced.
stories.impact: UC land acquisition in Westwood Village signals potential future repositioning of commercial assets adjacent to UCLA, but lack of disclosed strategy creates near-term uncertainty. If UC plans student/faculty housing, research facilities, or mixed-use development on this footprint, it could redirect local development economics and rental demand—but multifamily impact is speculative without further disclosure. Worth monitoring for zoning changes or master plan announcements.

stories.title: Mixed-Use Upper West Side Building Sells to Terra Developers for $28M
stories.excerpt: Brooklyn-based Terra Developers has made a $28 million residential redevelopment play for 500 Columbus Avenue on Manhattan’s Upper West Side. The 35,300-square-foot mixed-use building was sold to Terra by longtime owner CKMR Corporation, formerly Sloan’s Supermarkets, according to property records filed Friday. The property rises five stories at the northwest corner of West 84th Street and Columbus Avenue, just one block west of Central Park. Its ground-floor retail is anchored by a Gristedes supermarket, above which sits a dozen apartment units that have been vacant for 30 years, BKREA’s Bob Knakal told Commercial Observer. Knakal, the founder of BKREA and the exclusive listing agent for the property, said 500 Columbus Avenue’s residential spaces are well positioned for conversion into condominiums. An additional vertical expansion upon the 10,217-square-foot corner lot is possible, according to the BKREA listing. Yevgeniy Lvovskiy, CEO of ZHL Group, confirmed the purchase on behalf of Terra, but did not disclose Terra’s plans for the site. ZHL previously represented Terra and other investment partners in the $27.6 million purchase of a Long Island City, Queens, redevelopment site in 2024. The building at 500 Columbus Avenue was last sold in the 1970s to an entity of Sloan’s Supermarkets, founded by the Sloan and Meyer families. CKMR now manages legacy assets across New York City. Lucia Nuzzi-Meyer served as CKMR’s authorized signatory in the recent transaction. Representatives for CKMR could not immediately be reached for comment. Additional retail tenants at 500 Columbus Avenue include Park West Laundromat and a shoe repair shop. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Terra Developers acquires 500 Columbus Ave, Upper West Side, Manhattan for $28M mixed-use redevelopment.
35.3K SF, five-story building; 12 vacant residential units (empty 30 years); ground-floor Gristedes anchor.
Condo conversion and vertical expansion potential on corner lot one block from Central Park.
stories.summary: Terra Developers purchased 500 Columbus Avenue on Manhattan's Upper West Side for $28 million, a 35,300-square-foot, five-story mixed-use building at the corner of West 84th Street and Columbus Avenue. The property includes a ground-floor Gristedes supermarket and 12 apartment units that have been vacant for 30 years. BKREA's Bob Knakal cited condo conversion potential and possible vertical expansion on the 10,217-square-foot corner lot.
stories.impact: Signals emerging opportunity for residential redevelopment on Upper West Side as vacant-unit arbitrage and condo conversion economics improve in Manhattan's prime residential neighborhoods. Potential vertical expansion on underbuilt corner sites adjacent to Central Park indicates multifamily developers' confidence in pricing power and rental demand strength in this premium submarket, supporting feasibility of new supply in tight markets.

stories.title: CIP Real Estate Buys Broward Campus for $99M
stories.excerpt: CIP Real Estate has paid $99 million for an industrial and office park in Broward County, Fla., property records show. Called Lyons Business Park, the property includes about 10 buildings, totaling 338,000 square feet It’s located at 6601 Lyons Road in Coconut Creek, Fla., near the corner with Johnson Road, about a mile west of Florida’s Turnpike. BMO Bank, serving as an administrative agent for a group of lenders, supplied a $66.9 million acquisition loan, which is scheduled to mature in 2029. A vacant, 3,000-square-foot warehouse is currently on the market for $23 a square foot. The sellers, an entity tied to Tiffany and Lee Lasser and others, appear to have owned the 26-acre campus since the 1990s and early 2000s. The acquisition marks the second South Florida purchase for Irvine, Calif.-based CIP Real Estate in the past year, after it paid $47 million to acquire two small-bay warehouses in Hialeah from TA Realty. In 2024, the firm raised $300 million to expand its industrial footprint into the Southeast. Representatives for CIP Real Estate did not immediately respond to a request for comment, while the sellers could not be reached for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: CIP Real Estate acquires Lyons Business Park in Coconut Creek, Broward for $99M; 338K SF, ~10 buildings.
BMO Bank provides $66.9M acquisition loan (mature 2029); 26-acre industrial/office campus.
CIP's second South Florida purchase in 12 months; raised $300M in 2024 to expand Southeast industrial.
stories.summary: CIP Real Estate acquired Lyons Business Park in Coconut Creek, Florida for $99 million, comprising approximately 338,000 square feet across 10 buildings on a 26-acre campus. BMO Bank provided a $66.9 million acquisition loan maturing in 2029. The acquisition represents CIP's second South Florida purchase within 12 months and follows the firm's $300 million capital raise in 2024 to expand industrial footprint into the Southeast.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. CIP's aggressive South Florida industrial expansion (two acquisitions in 12 months, $300M capital deployment) reflects strong institutional conviction on Southeast industrial/logistics demand, likely driven by population migration to Florida and supply-chain regionalization. Multifamily developers should note competitive land acquisition and cost inflation in South Florida, especially in Broward/Miami-Dade, as industrial capital crowds the market.

stories.title: LMXD, BedRock Secure $250M Loan for 560-Unit Astoria Housing Project
stories.excerpt: LMXD and BedRock Real Estate Partners have closed on a $250 million loan to facilitate the purchase and construction of a housing development in Astoria, Queens, Commercial Observer has learned. The financing from New York Life Investment Management gets the wheels turning on the development of 560 mixed-income housing units at 35-10 Steinway Street, as well as a new retail location for a P.C. Richard & Son store in the neighborhood, according to the developers. “We are excited to move forward with our plan to bring mixed-income housing, including permanently affordable homes, to Steinway Street and contribute to the responsible growth of this vibrant neighborhood,” a spokesperson for LMXD and BedRock said in a statement. BedRock and LMXD acquired the site, which includes 35-18 Steinway Street, for $53 million last week. JLL‘s Rob Hinckley, Scott Aiese, Jeffrey Julien, Lauren Kaufman and Alex Staikos arranged the new financing for the transaction. “High-quality developments with strong sponsorship and solid fundamentals continue to attract institutional capital, and Steinway Crossing is a prime example,” Hinckley said in a statement. New York Life did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Apartment units in the Astoria project will range from studios to three-bedrooms, and 25 percent will be set aside as affordable housing for those earning an average of 60 percent of the area median income. The building will be designed by Beyer Blinder Belle Architects & Planners with all-electric infrastructure. However, the more interesting aspect of the development is that it falls within the section of land rezoned through a 2022 Uniform Land Use Review Procedure as part of the defunct Innovation QNS project by Silverstein Properties. bullets: LMXD and BedRock close $250M construction loan for 560-unit mixed-income development in Astoria, Queens.
Permanently affordable component; includes new P.C. Richard & Son retail; development at 35-10 Steinway Street.
New York Life Investment Management finances mixed-income housing on underutilized site in rapidly growing Queens neighborhood.
stories.summary: LMXD and BedRock Real Estate Partners closed a $250 million construction loan from New York Life Investment Management for a 560-unit mixed-income housing development at 35-10 Steinway Street in Astoria, Queens. The project includes permanently affordable units and new retail space for P.C. Richard & Son. The developers acquired the site (including 35-18 Steinway Street) for $53 million prior to securing financing.
stories.impact: Large institutional capital ($250M loan) flowing into mixed-income, affordable-component development in Queens (Astoria) signals strong lender appetite for workforce/affordable housing in rapidly gentrifying outer boroughs with transit access. Development economics support 560-unit project at density warranting new construction—validates Astoria's supply opportunity amid demand pressure from Manhattan spillover and transit access (N/W lines). Encourages similar mixed-income development in underutilized Queens sites with strong transit connectivity.
